title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Foot numbness and tingling.

HPI: The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a follow-up visit regarding chronic sensations in his lower extremities. He reports persistent tingling and a "pins and needles" feeling in both feet, which has become more pronounced over the last several months. He has a long-term history of type 2 diabetes and has been managing his blood glucose levels with a combination of injectable insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. He reports that the discomfort is constant but does not interfere with his ability to walk.

Medication List: Insulin, Metformin, Lisinopril.

Exam: Physical examination reveals intact sensation to light touch in the upper extremities. In the lower extremities, there is diminished sensation to monofilament testing in the hallux and first metatarsal head bilaterally. No visible ulcers or skin breakdown noted. Pedal pulses are palpable.

Assessment: 1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. 2. Peripheral neuropathy.

Plan: Continue current medication regimen of insulin and Metformin. Patient instructed to monitor foot health daily and report any new areas of skin breakdown immediately. Follow up in three months for further evaluation.
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
